To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perceived emotional intelligence predicts quality of life in older adults.

perceived emotional intelligence (PEI) predicts a significant percentage of the variance in older adults’ quality of life (Health, functional abilities, activity and leisure, life satisfaction), and that cognitive styles partially mediate this relationship.

perceived EI (PEQ) is associated with health, functional abilities, activity and leisure, and life satisfaction in institutionalized older adults and that this relationship can be explained by the mediating role of optimistic and pesimistic cognitive styles, with the latter being more important for the explanation of external QoL aspects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of EI for QoL in the elderly, and with its relationship with cognitive style, a factor that could explain some of the mechanisms involved in the IE and QoL relationship.
the importance of EI in older adults' health and well-being.
the importance of developing the emotional skills for healthy ageing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EI is an important predictor of QoL in older adults, and cognitive style partially mediates this association.

emotional intelligence and cognitive style are both important in older people's quality of life, and that the latter partially mediates the relationship between emotional intelligence and quality of life in older adults.
the PEI is associated with QoL in institutionalized older adults, and that cognitive styles partially mediate this relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional intelligence, as an important psychological resource in the elderly, could help to promote their quality of life.
the emotional intelligence of older adults can be a protective factor for their quality of life.
EI and its cognitive style components could be a useful tool to improve the QoL of institutionalized older adults, especially in the areas of health and personal well-being.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the promotion of emotional skills in older adults may contribute to the improvement of their health and quality of life.
EI can be an important tool to improve the QoL of institutionalized older adults.
the promotion of positive cognitive styles could help older adults with low EI to improve their QoL.
